title: Reduced post-transplant cyclophosphamide dose in patients undergoing haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for hematological malignancies: a phase III randomized study
official: Reduced post-transplant cyclophosphamide dose in patients undergoing haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for hematological malignancies: a phase III randomized study (REDUCy)
summary: Main objective: The primary objective is to evaluate the efficacy of reducing the total dose of PTCy to 70 mg/kg on GREFS compared to the standard dose of 100 mg/kg, in patients undergoing haploidentical HSCT for the treatment of a hematological malignancy, two years after HSCT.
conditions: The study will involve adult women and men from 16 French centers who have hematological malignancies and are candidates for haploidentical HSCT
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥ 18 years
2. Confirmed hematological malignancy with an indication for allogeneic HSCT
3. Presence of a haploidentical donor willing to donate PBSC
4. Patient planned to receive a thiotepa-based conditioning regimen
5. Provision of written informed consent
6. Affiliation to a social security system (excluding “Aide Médicale d’État”)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Karnofsky performance status < 70%
2. Individuals under legal protection measures or unable to provide consent (e.g., severe neurological or psychiatric disorders, or deprivation of liberty by judicial or administrative decision)
3. Hypersensitivity to the active substance or any of the excipients
4. Donor-specific anti-HLA antibodies requiring desensitization therapy prior to transplantation or otherwise considered by institutional standards to confer an unacceptable risk of graft failure.
5. Previous allo-HSCT
6. Participation to another interventional clinical trial except with the agreement of the coordinating investigator.
7. Inability to comply with study procedures
8. Life expectancy < 1 month, as determined by the inestigator
9. Acute or chronic heart failure, defined as left ventricular ejection fraction < 40%
10. Pulmonary dysfunction with hemoglobin-corrected diffusion capacity of carbon monoxide (DLCO) < 50% of predicted values, calculated according to the Dinakara method
11. Renal impairment with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 45 mL/min (calculated using the CKD-EPI formula)
12. Positive HIV status
13. Pregnancy, breast-feeding, or refusal to use effective contraception for at least 6 months after the last treatment dose
